scenes.headline: How a tiny model picks from any list
scenes.sub: cua-s1-forms: 706,048 parameters, one logit per option, trained from scratch.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Muffin! cua-s1-forms fills in forms with a tiny model, trained from scratch. Here's how it chooses.

scenes.text: Score every option on its own, then softmax over the scores. The head outputs one number, so the option list is data, not weights.
scenes.say: The idea: score each option alone. The head outputs one number, so the option list is data, not weights.

steps.say: The form and document go through a tiny byte-level encoder, two layers deep. The options are encoded separately.
Each option becomes a query against the context, and pulls out its own attended vector.
A shared dot product turns each pair into one logit. The head's output dimension is one.
Softmax runs over however many options the caller sent. Send two, send sixteen: the parameter count does not move.
Notice what's missing: no term compares one option with another.

scenes.title: Where the training data comes from
scenes.say: The dataset is entirely synthetic, built by three generators.

items.say: A random form of two to sixteen fields.
And a document padded with look-alikes, like email against street address, so the model must read the whole label.
Splits are disjoint by form, so a test form never shows up in training.

scenes.title: Two ways to answer from a list

left.title: Vocabulary readout
items: Options go in the prompt as lettered text
The model picks a letter token
Each letter carries its own learned prior
left.say: The other family lists options as letters in the prompt and reads the letter tokens. Each letter has its own prior.

right.title: Per-option scalar scorer
items: Each option encoded and scored alone
right.say: The scalar scorer has no letters and no positions, so order is not even expressible.

scenes.label: of openjev's decisions changed when the option order was reversed
scenes.say: Reverse the options for openjev, a letter readout, and ten of thirty-six decisions change.

scenes.text: A head that outputs one number per option makes the option list data, and its order irrelevant.
scenes.say: So one number per option makes the list data, and its order irrelevant.

recap: A byte encoder, 706,048 parameters, from scratch
Each option queries the context: one logit each
No letters, so option order cannot matter
scenes.say: To recap: a tiny encoder, one logit per option, and no letters for order to cling to.
